diagnosis: The 0.2.0 A-share product already had strong point-in-time freeze, P01-P09 research, Tonghuashun/Level-2 preference, Xuangutong five-pool reconciliation, U0/U1/U3 lineage, immutable review and replay-governed learning. A generic multi-agent rewrite was unnecessary and would reduce domain specialization.

The 0.2.0 internal graph placed EVENT_ALPHA, MARKET_STRUCTURE and BUYABILITY_EXECUTION inside one competitive-candidate group. That incorrectly allowed risk/executability to behave like another opinion rather than a constraint/veto layer.

The post-close contract mechanically graded research recall but did not give frozen final recommendations an equally strict activation/outcome/execution-feasibility scorecard, creating an optimization bias toward finding more opportunities rather than selecting executable recommendations well.
User-facing reports did not expose the new risk assurance/veto and selection-quality evidence until the final candidate hardening pass.
governing_assumptions_rejected: Risk/buyability is just a third candidate opinion that may be outvoted by two opportunity views.
Improved U1 recall is sufficient evidence that a recommendation-rule change improved the product.
A recommendation whose trigger never fired should be counted like an executed win/loss.
A strong opportunity narrative may retain FULL execution assurance when preferred microstructure evidence is missing.
The A-share product should be redesigned around the same internal topology as the Video product.

external_method_research.source: QuantConnect Algorithm Framework — Alpha / Portfolio / Risk / Execution separation
external_method_research.finding: Risk and execution operate as distinct downstream control concerns rather than additional alpha signals.
external_method_research.adopted_as: Opportunity views compete first; every U1 candidate receives an explicit risk/feasibility assessment; BLOCK cannot enter U3.

external_method_research.source: CFA Institute — Trade Strategy and Execution
external_method_research.finding: Trade decisions must account for expected alpha together with liquidity, volatility, market impact, costs and execution risk.
external_method_research.adopted_as: Execution assurance and post-close feasibility are explicit product dimensions instead of being hidden inside opportunity ranking.

external_method_research.finding: Evaluation should examine multiple risk/return dimensions and regimes rather than optimize one success metric.
external_method_research.adopted_as: Replay PASS must report recall, activated-positive, activated-downside and execution-feasibility metrics across frozen multi-regime cases.

external_method_research.source: Python language reference — starred expression/list display syntax
external_method_research.finding: Iterable unpacking requires a valid operand expression; compressed report construction introduced an invalid starred/or expression.
external_method_research.adopted_as: Use explicit intermediate report-line variables; keep delivery code readable rather than compressing expressions.

candidate_failure_evidence.resolution: Recovery fixture now follows CURRENT_CONTRACT_VERSION; valid Replay PASS fixture now supplies all decision-quality metrics. No production constraint was weakened.
External Python syntax check plus assumption review; replaced compressed starred/or report expression with explicit intermediate list. No business rule changed.
